definitions.explanation: The final part or outcome of a story, event, or situation. Often implies a resolution or settlement. Composed of 結 (tie, conclude) + 末 (end).

examples.japanese: {結末|けつまつ}が{気|き}になる。
この{小説|しょうせつ}の{結末|けつまつ}には{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I was surprised by the ending of this novel.

examples.japanese: {事件|じけん}は{思|おも}いがけない{結末|けつまつ}を{迎|むか}え、{関係者|かんけいしゃ}{全員|ぜんいん}が{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: The case reached an unexpected conclusion, surprising everyone involved.

notes:
USAGE:
{結末|けつまつ} refers to the conclusion or final outcome of events, stories, or situations. It is commonly used when discussing narratives (novels, movies, dramas) as well as real-life events.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {結末|けつまつ}を{迎|むか}える (to reach a conclusion)
- {意外|いがい}な{結末|けつまつ} (unexpected ending)
- {悲|かな}しい{結末|けつまつ} (sad ending)
- ハッピーエンドの{結末|けつまつ} (happy ending)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{結果|けっか} means result or outcome and is more general. {結末|けつまつ} specifically implies the final resolution of a sequence of events. {終結|しゅうけつ} means conclusion or termination and is more formal.
